findings.title: Reusable DRBG session is not terminal after every exceptional state transition
findings.standardsReference: NIST SP 800-90A Rev. 1 sections 8.8 and 10.1.2.5; implementation state-protection and fail-closed policy
findings.consequence: A non-canonical caller that catches a state-transition exception could reuse a changed session. One direct V replacement leaves the prior managed array for garbage collection rather than immediately zeroing it.
findings.exploitability: Minimal in the canonical provider because its finally block always destroys the per-draw session and no result is accepted after an exception. Misuse requires a future direct in-process caller outside the canonical wrapper.
findings.remediation: In a separate narrow package, zero the replaced V in the Generate loop and terminally destroy or invalidate a session after an exception that may follow state mutation. Add fault-injection tests for pre-update, block generation, continuous-test, post-update, and output-hash failures.
findings.certificationRelevance: External reviewers commonly inspect exceptional-path state custody and API misuse resistance. Close before formal specialist or laboratory review.

findings.title: Cancellation may omit terminal non-authoritative attempt evidence
findings.standardsReference: Mosera immutable evidence and fail-closed operational audit requirements
findings.consequence: A cancellation after a durable execution claim but before completion may leave no explicit canceled attempt row, reducing audit completeness and recovery diagnosis.
findings.exploitability: Low. Cancellation creates no fallback result, certificate, outcome, settlement, or financial effect; locks and session secrets are released. The gap is evidence completeness, not output authority.
findings.remediation: Append a distinct canceled attempt with a bounded non-request cancellation token before propagating cancellation, while preserving the original cancellation reason and never accepting output.
findings.certificationRelevance: Likely to be noted where immutable execution-attempt evidence is an asserted control. Close before external review.

findings.title: Unused generic security-strength and hash profiles expand review scope
findings.standardsReference: NIST SP 800-90A Rev. 1 selected mechanism and security-strength profile
findings.consequence: SHA-384/SHA-512 and 128/192 profiles require extra review if included in a certification boundary even though production uses only SHA-256/256.
findings.exploitability: No authority bypass was found; the production provider hardcodes SHA-256/256.
findings.remediation: Define the certified production boundary as SHA-256/256 or narrow the production-facing runtime in a future package. Do not claim unused profiles as qualified without evidence.

findings.title: No remediated digest-pinned production image is frozen
findings.standardsReference: External review module-boundary and supply-chain evidence
findings.consequence: The current local image predates remediation and Docker base tags are mutable, so source review cannot yet be tied to an immutable deployable artifact.
findings.exploitability: No defect in the reviewed source. Risk appears during release packaging or dependency drift.
findings.remediation: Build from the reviewed commit, pin base image digests, capture runtime/package inventory, SBOM, image digest, and provenance attestation.
findings.certificationRelevance: Required for a coherent external module package and production release evidence.

findings.title: SP 800-90B entropy validation is not established
findings.consequence: Successful OS byte requests and byte-length checks do not prove source min-entropy, physical-source health, or a validated entropy boundary.
findings.exploitability: Depends on platform, kernel, VM, and host compromise. Application logic cannot independently repair a compromised source.
findings.remediation: Obtain platform/module entropy documentation and validation evidence, or define a validated entropy-source integration for the certification boundary.
findings.certificationRelevance: External dependency for formal entropy claims.

findings.title: Formal SP 800-90C construction classification lacks evidence
source: CSPRNG-1.3C conformance matrix and entropy boundary assessment
findings.consequence: The construction is structurally closest to RBG2, but formal conformance cannot be stated without entropy and module-boundary evidence.
findings.exploitability: Claiming conformance prematurely would create assurance and regulatory risk; no runtime exploit follows from the classification gap itself.
findings.remediation: Retain `SP800_90C_CLASSIFICATION_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` until the entropy and module boundary are externally established.

findings.title: Managed-runtime physical erasure and host hardening remain external boundaries
findings.standardsReference: NIST SP 800-90A Rev. 1 state protection; deployment security boundary
findings.consequence: GC movement, JIT temporaries, HMAC internals, crash dumps, debuggers, and a compromised host can retain or expose state despite best-effort zeroization.
findings.exploitability: Requires process/host privilege or memory compromise and is outside the application-only threat boundary.
findings.remediation: Use hardened hosts, disable or encrypt dumps, restrict ptrace/debug, minimize process privilege, and document managed-runtime limitations. Consider a validated module/HSM boundary only if required by certification goals.
findings.certificationRelevance: Must be documented in external threat and deployment reviews.

internalExcellenceGate.rationale: No CRITICAL, HIGH, or MEDIUM finding remains. Both LOW findings have minimal exploitability in the canonical path, preserve fail-closed authority, and have narrow remediations assigned before external review.
